fields.v: Jiang, Z., Deng, L., Cao, J., Pradel, M., Liu, Z. (2026). Doc2Feat-Bench: Evaluating Documentation-Driven Feature Addition. In: Proceedings of the 41st IEEE/ACM International Conference on Automated Software Engineering (ASE '26), Munich, Germany, ACM. https://doi.org/10.1145/3832783.3837489. Read from arXiv:2507.18130v4 [cs.SE], 3 Aug 2026 (earlier versions titled NoCode-bench)

Conference — ASE 2026 (41st IEEE/ACM International Conference on Automated Software Engineering), ACM, DOI 10.1145/3832783.3837489; full text read from arXiv:2507.18130v4, which carries the ASE reference format

Zhejiang University, College of Computer Science and Technology and State Key Laboratory of Blockchain and Data Security, China (Jiang, Deng, Liu); Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Cao); CISPA Helmholtz Center for Information Security, Germany (Pradel)

Proposes an evaluation method; secondary: Compares — new benchmark (Doc2Feat-Bench, 634 tasks; Verified subset of 114) for documentation-driven feature addition, used to compare 8 LLMs with two scaffolds (Agentless, OpenHands)

No SDD approach evaluated. Setting: documentation-driven feature addition (documentation diff as the feature specification; authors cite README-driven development, OpenAPI workflows and spec-driven development / GitHub Spec Kit as documentation-first practices). Scaffolds evaluated: Agentless-1.0 (pipeline-based) and OpenHands CodeAct Agent (agent-based; version not stated)

Task input: the documentation change (diff of public-facing docs) plus the full codebase at the base commit; optional identifier hints (undocumented, test-referenced entity names); PR numbers/URLs masked. Expected output: a code patch

Not prescribed for the agent. Agentless: hierarchical localization (files, classes/methods, lines) then patch generation with post-processing; OpenHands: model-driven tool use in a sandbox. Benchmark construction in five phases: project selection, instance collection, environment construction, instance filtering, input refinement
None in the agent runs (autonomous). Humans only in benchmark construction: manual environment fixes and annotation of the Verified subset (two annotators per task)
Specification format only: the documentation diff used as the task input to autonomous scaffolds; no SDD workflow run
Not classifiable (no SDD approach; authors' wording: 'documentation updates act as executable, public-facing feature specifications that software engineering agents translate into code changes')
Existing code bases: feature addition in mature open-source projects

Full: 634 tasks from 10 projects (from 3,263 PRs, 1,571 candidates), about 114k code changes in total; golden patches on average 2.65 files, 10.32 hunks, 179.12 changed lines; 13.56% need new files. Verified: 114 tasks; 2.39 files, 8.96 hunks, 179.22 lines. Mean documentation-change length 739.06 (Full) and 820.65 (Verified), unit not stated
Python open-source libraries, developer tools and frameworks (10 of the 12 SWE-bench projects, e.g. astropy, matplotlib, scikit-learn, seaborn, pylint, pytest; flask and sympy excluded)
N/A (autonomous agents, no participants). Verified-subset annotators: five, with at least three years of Python and a bachelor's degree or higher
#Token: average token cost per instance. Estimated cost of running four models on Full: USD 5,124 (reason for not running them)

Success% (patch passes the accompanying tests); Applied% (patch applies); RT% (regression tests, P2P, all pass); Feature Validation Rate FV-Micro (passed F2P tests over all F2P tests) and FV-Macro (mean per-instance F2P pass rate), new metric
None
None

File% (file matched rate between model-edited and reference files); single-file vs multi-file success (Table 6); failure categories from manual analysis of 160 failed runs; Levenshtein similarity of successful patches to ground truth (leakage check, mean 0.48)

Automatic: patches applied and tests run in per-project Docker images with conda environments; F2P/P2P test sets from before/after logs; token counts. Manual: failure analysis of 160 failed instances (10 per model per scaffold) from execution traces; Verified subset annotated by two annotators per task (Cohen's kappa 0.4193); filtered-instance analysis by two authors (kappa 0.932 and 0.913)

Tasks: Doc2Feat-Bench Verified (114) for 8 models x 2 scaffolds; Full (634) for 4 models with Agentless only (cost). Configurations: model x scaffold. Baseline: none formal; SWE-bench scores of the same model/scaffold used as reference (e.g. Claude-4-Sonnet + OpenHands 70.4% on SWE-bench Verified; Qwen3-Coder + OpenHands 69.60% on SWE-bench). Held constant: task inputs (documentation diff, masked references), evaluation Docker images, test oracle. Acceptance tests: developer-written F2P and P2P tests. Repetitions: Not stated (single run implied). Human intervention: none. Whether identifier hints were given in the experiments: Not stated

Verified: best Qwen3-Coder-480B + OpenHands 37.72%, then GPT-5-mini + OpenHands 36.84%; Gemini-2.5-Pro + OpenHands 0%. Agentless better on average than OpenHands: success 20.94 vs 16.45, Applied 98.80 vs 67.98, RT 76.97 vs 62.06, FV-Micro 8.74 vs 4.92, FV-Macro 31.25 vs 23.35, File% 51.56 vs 46.23, tokens 0.29M vs 1.15M (OpenHands context overflow gives incomplete or empty patches). Full: four-model average success falls from 18.20% (Verified) to 10.65%, best DeepSeek-R1 14.83%; rankings largely preserved except Qwen3-235B vs GPT-4o. Multi-file tasks: best 20.75% (Verified) and 6.40% (Full). Far below SWE-bench results. No significance tests

Distinguished models and scaffolds (0% to 37.72%) and showed a gap to SWE-bench; model rankings largely consistent between Verified and Full, taken by the authors as support for validity. Repeatability not assessed (no repeated runs). Limitations stated: task quality (incomplete docs, partial tests; 124 of 238 sampled candidates, 52.1%, filtered), data leakage risk, Python-only projects with structured release notes, only two scaffolds

Limitations: documentation changes may be incomplete and tests may not fully cover the feature (mitigated by Verified subset); possible data leakage (PR numbers masked; mean Levenshtein similarity 0.48); only Python projects with feature-labelled release notes; only Agentless and OpenHands scaffolds. Gaps: agents' cross-file editing, understanding of existing code modules (39.38% of examined failures break existing features), and interpretation of documentation semantics (exceptions 33.13%, edge conditions 20.00%, unspecified invalid input 7.88%); extension to other languages

Inconsistencies: Fig. 5 labels the golden patch of a pylint task with path '/django/forms/models.py' (p. 10); FV-Micro on Full (Table 5) is higher than on Verified (Table 4) for three of the four models (Qwen3-235B 8.75 to 10.78, DeepSeek-v3 7.96 to 16.02, GPT-4o 7.97 to 8.68) while their success rates fall, not discussed (p. 8-9); the failure-analysis percentages (39.38%, 33.13%, 20.00%, 7.88%) have no stated denominator and 7.88% is not a whole number of the 160 examined instances (12.6) (p. 9-10); Table 4 values were rebuilt from a garbled text extraction (columns split across lines) and should be checked against the PDF (p. 8). 'About 114k code changes' unit not defined (p. 1). Data: replication package and online appendix at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21762257; repository https://github.com/Doc2Feat-bench/Doc2Featbench; leaderboard http://doc2featbench.org (p. 12). No pre-registration. Programming language: Python

rev.why: The draft said FV-Micro is above FV-Macro in Table 5 for three of four models; in Table 5 FV-Micro is below FV-Macro for all four (e.g. 10.78 vs 15.77). The real oddity is FV-Micro rising from Verified to Full for three models while success falls
Missing inconsistency added: the failure-category percentages in RQ3 have no stated denominator, and 7.88% does not correspond to a whole count of the 160 examined failures (p. 9-10)
